Editor.problem: The load rate in the brief is probably wrong. telemetrygen `traces` sends a parent and a child span per trace by default (--child-spans is 1), and --rate=15 with --workers=4 is 60 traces a second. With --batch=false that is likely about 120 single-span requests a second, not 60. The open question, the takeaway and every queue-capacity argument (1000 requests vs 40 s of load) depend on that rate, and nothing in the plan measures it.
Editor.fix: Add --child-spans=0 to k8s/20-load.yaml, or keep the default and change the brief to the real rate. Either way, add a measurement `gateway_accept_rate` (accepted spans per second over the 10 s before the outage, from two counter reads) for all 6 runs, so the stated rate comes from the lab and not from the flags.

Editor.problem: The title promises to 'Count Every Span Through an Outage', but there is no count from the sender. --allow-export-failures plus the SDK's own retries mean refused counts attempts, not spans. Spans the sender gave up on, or dropped at shutdown when the 60 s load ended, appear in no counter. accepted − sent can be 0 while spans were still lost before the gateway.
Editor.fix: Count from the sender: give each run's spans a unique label (lab.run already exists) and count unique spans that reach the relay or Splunk per run. Or read telemetrygen's own sent and failed totals from its log into a measurement `load_spans_generated` and compare it with accepted for all 6 runs. Without that, retitle to what the counters show (accepted, refused, delivered).

Editor.problem: lost() adds refused and enqueue_failed. In the migrated config, a span the full queue rejects is counted once in otelcol_exporter_enqueue_failed_spans and again in otelcol_receiver_refused_spans, because the error goes back to the receiver. Refused also counts sender retries. The summed figure double-counts and isn't a span count, yet the reproduce check and any article table would use it as 'spans lost'.
Editor.fix: Don't sum them. Report refused and enqueue_failed as separate columns, and base reproduce.sh's check on enqueue_failed > 0 (migrated) and enqueue_failed = 0 (batch). Write in the brief that refused counts attempts, and say which component's error reached the client in each config.

Editor.problem: seconds_to_drain and spans_not_delivered treat queue_size = 0 as 'drained'. The queue-size metric excludes requests the exporter's consumers hold while they retry. The default retry_on_failure backoff grows up to a 30 s interval, so after a 40 s outage some batches may wait close to 30 s before their next try. DRAIN_MAX=30 starts after the load ends, and the final read comes 3 s after the queue reads 0. Spans still in retry would show up as 'not delivered' and be charged to the config.
Editor.fix: Define drained as sent increasing to equal accepted (with queue_size 0 and sent unchanged across two reads), not queue_size alone. Raise DRAIN_MAX to at least 90 s, and record send_failed and queue_size at the final read. Log the effective retry_on_failure and num_consumers for each config with the printed configs.

Editor.problem: splunk_apm_spans is compared with the gateway's sent count over different windows. apm_spans reads [t_load, t_end] (load start to load end). The gateway's sent count runs to the end of the drain, and spans queued during the outage arrive after t_end. If APM places spans.count by arrival time, outage runs undercount and look like data loss. It isn't the same window, counted the same way.
Editor.fix: Write the drain-end time (time of the gw-end read) into runs.txt and read APM from t_load to drain end + 20 s, rounded out to whole 10 s points. Make sure windows of runs next to each other don't overlap (add a 30 s gap between runs). Compare APM with relay_accepted, the same spans one step downstream, as well as with gateway sent, and report the difference rather than asserting equality.

Marketing.problem: The brief and the measurement list promise Splunk APM span counts for all six runs (batch-1, batch-2, migrated-1, migrated-2, sized-1, sized-2). The lab only reads spans.count in fix.sh, so the sized runs alone would have it. The 'spans a backend holds' angle is the stated gap in existing pages, and it would be missing for the before and after runs. It is also the Splunk tie-in that supports the Splunk MVP goal.
Marketing.fix: Read the Splunk APM span count for every run, with a unique run tag or a separate window per run so the counts don't overlap. Add a wait for ingest lag before reading. If that can't be done, drop splunk_apm_spans from the promise and the 'adds' line, and let the Collector counters carry the story.

Marketing.problem: The title is an instruction followed by a claim, 'Count Every Span'. It doesn't name the pain the reader just hit, and it leaves out the words they would search for: 'batch processor deprecated', 'sending_queue', 'exporter batching'. The promise is also loose. The plan measures counts, so it can't show that every span survives unless the sized config really delivers all of them. Refused spans can be retried by the sender, so the counts are attempts.
Marketing.fix: Retitle around the reader's trigger and the gain, for example: 'Batch Processor Deprecated? Move Batching Into the Exporter and Keep Every Span Through a Backend Outage'. Keep the 'keep every span' promise only if sized-1 and sized-2 each deliver every accepted span. Otherwise promise 'size the queue so an outage doesn't cost you spans' and report the measured numbers.
